claims.statement: Poland's climate ministry reports about 1.631 million prosumers by April 2026 and 127386 prosumer batteries by March 2026, indicating a large installed base and an emerging controllable-storage segment.

Official guidance says self-consumption and battery management are central to net-billing economics and specifically describes shifting device use and charging or discharging in response to production and hourly prices.
A government priority page targets 200000 home energy-storage systems by the end of 2027 and reported two support programmes in development or approval as of March 2026.

contrary_evidence: Many inverters, batteries and smart-home systems already include free scheduling and monitoring apps.
Official guidance presents simple behavioural scheduling that may capture much of the value without paid optimisation.
A large prosumer count does not show that household savings are large enough to sustain monthly software fees.

economics.acquisition_route: Connect one inverter family and 30-50 volunteered sites from the family company, measure bill-normalised lift in shadow mode, then sell wholesalers a co-branded installer retention product.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Forty thousand sites averaging 15 PLN net monthly revenue would produce 7.2m PLN recurring annual revenue before diagnostics and referrals. At a mature 42% owner-cash margin, about 3.02m PLN per year could yield more than 10m PLN cumulative distributions over five mature years without assuming a sale.
economics.founder_time: Support one inverter protocol and advisory reports at 3-4 hours/day, with all device changes executed by qualified installers; keep employment until multi-installer repeat demand and contribution margin are proven.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Data ingestion, forecasts and reports are software-heavy; target 75-88% gross margin on licences and diagnostics, excluding any pass-through hardware or on-site labour.
economics.payback: Target installer payback within one converted retrofit or reduced diagnostic truck roll; homeowner payback depends on measured bill savings and is not yet known.
economics.pricing: Assumption to test: installer licence of 15-35 PLN per monitored site monthly, a 300-700 PLN homeowner diagnostic, and a transparent 1-3% referral fee on qualified storage or control retrofits.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Energy data and bills recur continuously, while new tariffs, seasons and devices refresh recommendations; low savings or closed OEM ecosystems can cause churn.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A device-protocol library and longitudinal Polish load, weather, tariff and intervention-response dataset improve counterfactual savings estimates and configuration recommendations.
fingerprint.customer: Polish installers with hundreds of residential prosumer sites, initially those combining PV with batteries, heat pumps or EV charging.
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Pilot on the founder's family installer base, then distribute via inverter/battery wholesalers and installer buying groups; homeowner acquisition remains owned by installers.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: White-label data layer that imports meter/inverter history, forecasts solar and controllable load, simulates tariff-aware schedules and retrofit ROI, then issues a verified savings report; SaaS per monitored site plus qualified-install referral revenue.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The installer pays a wholesale per-site monitoring licence and the prosumer pays for an optimisation audit or premium monitoring; existing paid events are the electricity bill, service call and hardware retrofit.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A customer receives a disappointing electricity bill, considers a battery/EMS retrofit, or asks the installer whether existing equipment is scheduled optimally under net-billing.

founder_fit: The family renewable-energy business offers a trusted installed-base pilot and installer-language feedback.
Forecasting, optimisation and counterfactual measurement are strong data-science problems.
Installer-owned distribution avoids direct mass-market support and public-persona marketing.
An advisory-only first version limits hardware and safety liability while remaining testable alongside employment.
risks: Bad advice could shorten battery life, reduce comfort or increase bills.
OEM API closure can strand integrations.
Savings claims require transparent baselines to avoid consumer-protection problems.
A mass homeowner support burden would conflict with the founder's time and interaction preferences.

structure.commercial_archetype: Installer-channel energy-analytics SaaS with retrofit referral upside
structure.control_point: The verified baseline and ROI report used to schedule equipment and approve a battery, EMS or heat-pump control change
structure.critical_dependency: Reliable inverter/meter data access and enough flexible household load for recommendations to create measurable savings

thesis: Give Polish PV, battery and heat-pump installers a vendor-neutral monitoring and recommendation layer that uses meter, inverter, tariff and weather data to show where each customer's net-billing value is lost and which schedule or retrofit produces a defensible payback. Prosumers already pay electricity bills and buy energy hardware; installers gain recurring revenue and better-qualified battery or EMS upsells from their installed base.
title: White-Label PV Self-Consumption Optimizer for Installers
uncertainties: Accessible APIs, data quality and remote-control permissions vary by equipment vendor.
The incremental savings over OEM defaults and simple schedules have not been measured on Polish bills.
Installer willingness to pay for ongoing monitoring rather than one-off hardware margin is unknown.
Pricing, margins, adoption scale and wealth projections are assumptions.
